instructions: Dice the onion and mince the garlic. Rinse the lentils. Peel the potatoes and carrots, cut the potatoes into 1/2 inch cubes, and slice the carrots into thin half moons.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook, stirring now and then, for 5 minutes, until it's soft but not brown.
Add the garlic and coriander and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell them.
Add the lentils, the potatoes, the carrots and 6 cups water. Bring it to a boil over high heat, then cover and turn the heat to medium-low. Simmer for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash the chard. Chop the stems small and cut the leaves into thin strips, keeping them separate.
Add the chard stems and 1 tsp of the salt to the pot. Cover and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the chard leaves. Cover and simmer for 5 minutes, until the lentils and potatoes are soft and the leaves are wilted.
Juice the lemons. That should be about 1/3 cup. Stir it into the soup off the heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lemon.
Serve the soup in bowls with a drizzle of the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.
method_notes: The Salt & Sweet version cooks brown lentils with onion, potatoes, carrots and Swiss chard and adds the lemon at the end. It simmers the lentils first and adds the vegetables later, and offers a cornstarch slurry to thicken. This version adds the lentils, potatoes and carrots together, with the potatoes cut small, to keep the soup inside 45 minutes, and skips the slurry because the potato thickens it. Garlic and coriander are the traditional Lebanese seasoning for this soup. It uses water only, so it stays vegan and gluten-free.
